findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. Minimal dust accumulation on the fans in the walk-in cooler. Keep fans clean so soiled air does not move through space/hang over cooling foods. Discussed cleaning beneath the sinks in the preparation room to support elimiation of pests. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw shell eggs stored above cooked pulled pork (prep cooler bottom)
The PIC was informed and the raw items were moved. A handout was also provided for the purposes of educating staff. Ensure staff are never storing raw meat (including egg) above ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw shell eggs stored above cooked pulled pork (prep cooler bottom)
2. Raw hamburger stored above ketchup and mustard (prep cooler bottom)
3. Raw hamburger stored above margarine (walk-in cooler)
4. Raw shell egg stored above produce (walk-in cooler)

The PIC was informed and the raw items were moved. A handout was also provided for the purposes of educating staff. Ensure staff are never storing raw meat (including egg) above ready-to-eat foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed excessive food splash and rust on walls/floor of walk-in cooler. Informed PIC that non-food contact surfaces of cooler need to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent soil and pathogen accumulation. Rust accumulation creates pits and dents in surface, allowing for bacteria and other pathogens to accumulate. Ensure walk-in cooler is repaired by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizer solution available in kitchen to test at 10 ppm Cl-. Sanitizer solution was remade during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed floors behind chest freezers in back room to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize floors behind chest freezers. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed employee rinse out coffee pot in kitchen hand washing sink. Use hand washing sinks only for the purpose of hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed in-use tongs stored with food contact surface touching handle of container on steam table. Tongs were moved during inspection. Store in-use utensils on a clean food contact surface.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed area above grill and fryers used to store dish ware and to-go boats to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize area above grill and fryers. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed certified food manager on duty to have an additional allergen certification that has expired. Renew additional allergen training certification.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed 4 recently cooled or opened items with no date marking. Best practice is to date mark all unused TCS/ready to eat items at the end of the day. This way items are easily identified by inspection staff as intentionally cooled and kept and not as improperly date marked. Dates were added to the items immediately. 3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on a gallon of whole milk in the walk in cooler. Employee states that the milk was opened on Wednesday. The milk was properly date marked. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11. Observed a grey sweat shirt to be in the shelves in front under the coffee station. There are single use packets of condiments stored under this area as well. The sweat shirt was removed.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all hand washing sinks used by food employees. Sign missing at the women's restroom. Provide a clearly visible hand washing sign at each hand sink. Sign was provided immediately. Reference 6-301.14.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surface (cardboard) usde in the freezer is not easily cleanable. Replace cardboard box used for storage with a nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Cheese sauce in the walk in cooler is 51F. There is no time tag for cooling on the container. Time tag was added. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Observed chili beef on ice in the back with in internal temperature of 100F.  The beef was put to cool at 2pm according to employee. There is not a temperature log to know what temperature the chili beef was when placed on ice. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. The Chili beef was also in quantities greater than four inches. Suggest stirring the items to be cooled and keeping a temperature log of the cooling process.  The beef was broken down into shallow pans and placed into the chest  freezers. The chili beef will be kept. Chili beef is in 50F range by 4:20pm.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Observed tray of donuts on the counter at the serving line. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Protect these with somr sort of cover.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Dust and grease were beginning to accumulate on the hood baffles over the grill and fryers. Clean the baffles as needed to eliminate buildup of dust/grease.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled with general debris under the soda machine at the drive thru and along the walls behind chest freezers. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee worked the cash register/handled money and did not wash hands prior to unwrapping and stocking single service items (cup lids by drive thru window). Employee was observed washing hands upon entering the food service area; however, employee was advised hands must be washed again before handling single service articles, food and clean equipment after working the cash register.
Handwashing was discussed with employee and owner.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and immediately before engaging in food preparation, including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Back handsink across from 3 part sink was blocked. Large Oscar Meyer Weiner boxes were stacked on top of the basin inhibiting access for handwashing. An employee removed the boxes from the area at the request of inspector.
Handsinks shall be accessible to employees at all times to allow for proper handwashing. Do not block handsinks with boxes, equipment, and/or other materials.
